note_claims.claim: Two to three episodes per month.
Followed by unilateral, usually left-sided, throbbing headache with nausea and photophobia.
No focal weakness, numbness or speech disturbance.
Not worse on lying down, coughing or straining.
Stop combined pill; start desogestrel 75 micrograms once daily continuously.
Use condoms for the first 2 days of desogestrel.
Sumatriptan 50 mg at headache onset (not during aura).
Sumatriptan may repeat after 2 hours, maximum 600 mg in 24 hours.
Limit acute treatment to 2–3 days per week to avoid medication-overuse headache.
Call 999 or attend A&E if sudden severe headache, one-sided weakness or numbness, speech difficulty, or headache with fever and neck stiffness.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reports getting headaches and they are getting more frequent.
Headaches have been occurring for about six months.
Headaches occur maybe two or three times a month.
Headaches start with vision symptoms, specifically zigzag lines, shimmering, off to one side.
The duration of the zigzag vision symptoms was about an hour.
Correction: The duration of the zigzag vision symptoms was actually twenty minutes, not an hour.
The headache comes on one side, usually the left, and it throbs.
Patient feels sick and cannot stand bright lights, requiring them to lie down in a dark room.
The headache lasts most of the day, and the patient is wiped out the next day.
The patient reports no weakness, numbness, or trouble speaking with the headaches.
Patient has never had a sudden, severe headache (like being hit on the head) the worst ever.
Headaches are not worse when the patient lies down, coughs, or strains.
Patient reports no fevers or stiff neck.
The patient's mother has migraines without aura.
Patient is currently taking paracetamol, but it does not do much.
Patient is taking Rigevidon (combined oral contraceptive) and has been on it for about four years.
Patient does not smoke.
Patient reports no known drug allergies.
Blood pressure is 118 over 76.
The back of the eyes look normal.
The nervous system examination is completely normal.
The clinician diagnoses the condition as migraines with aura, with the zigzags being the aura.
Migraine itself is not dangerous, but combined pill use increases the risk of stroke.
The clinician plans to stop Rigevidon and switch to desogestrel 75 micrograms, one every day without a break.
The clinician advises using condoms for the first two days after starting desogestrel.
The clinician prescribes sumatriptan 50 milligrams for headaches, to be taken as soon as the headache starts (not during zigzags).
If the headache returns, the patient can take another dose after two hours, but no more than 300 milligrams in 24 hours.
Sumatriptan can be taken with paracetamol.
The clinician advises limiting the use of painkillers or sumatriptan to more than two or three days a week to avoid medication-overuse headache.
The clinician advises keeping a headache diary.
The follow-up appointment is scheduled in six weeks.
Safety-netting advice: Call 999 or go to A&E if there is a sudden severe headache, one-sided weakness or numbness, speech difficulty, or a headache with fever and a stiff neck.

findings.note_span: Sumatriptan may repeat after 2 hours, maximum 600 mg in 24 hours.
findings.transcript_evidence: If the headache comes back, you can take another after two hours, but no more than 300 milligrams in 24 hours.
findings.rationale: The note incorrectly documents the maximum repeat dose of sumatriptan as 600 mg, whereas the transcript correctly states the maximum is 300 mg in 24 hours, which is a significant dosing error.
